view.opacityTip: How solid the route's lines and arrows are on the editor's map. Lower lets more of the map show through; the numbered points stay as they are.
view.showTip:
All, faded: with a point selected, the route is shown as the player will see it from there. The leg into the point and the steps after it are bright, the rest is faded and without arrows. With nothing selected the whole route is drawn in full.
All: the whole route in full, whatever is selected.
Every point is always drawn: the editor has no “steps” choice, as the overlay does.
view.aheadTip: How many steps from the selected point are bright, with their arrows. The first is the leg into the point itself.

settings.advancedHint: The defaults suit most maps. Change one thing at a time.
settings.confirmReset: Put every setting back to its default, the language and the options for route progress and the checklist included? Routes, maps, the map area, your progress along each route and the update settings are kept.
settings.detectInterval: How often to refine the anchor
settings.languageTip: The language of the panel, the editor and the checklist. System follows the language of Windows.
settings.fpsTip:
How many frames a second the app captures and looks at. More follows the map more smoothly and costs more processor time.
Keep it at or above the game's own frame rate, or the route lags behind the map.
settings.opacityTip: How solid the route drawn over the game is: its lines, arrows and numbered points. Lower lets more of the map show through.
settings.routeViewTip:
Steps: only the route around you. The next steps bright, the last ones passed faded, nothing else. The easiest to follow when a route loops about.
All, faded: the whole route, bright only for the next steps and faded everywhere else.
All: the whole route ahead bright, what was passed faded.
settings.routeAheadTip: How many steps ahead are drawn bright, with their arrows. The leg you are walking now is the first of them.
settings.routePastTip: How many steps already passed stay on the checklist, and on the map in the Steps view, faded, so you can see where you came from. None leaves them out.
settings.trackingTip:
By motion: the overlay follows how the picture moves from one frame to the next, and full detection only corrects it now and then. Smooth and light.
Detection only: every frame is matched against the map from scratch. Heavier, and it can jitter, but it never drifts.
settings.detectIntervalTip: With tracking by motion: how often full detection checks where the map is and corrects the drift. More often corrects sooner and costs more.
settings.smoothingTip: How gently the overlay is pulled toward each new result of detection. More takes the shake out but trails behind a quick pan. Off follows every result at once.
settings.transformTip:
Pan, zoom, rotate suits a flat map such as the game's and is the steadier of the two.
Any perspective also allows for tilt, for a map shown at an angle. It can wobble on a flat one.
settings.detectorTip:
Accurate (SIFT) finds the map reliably, zoomed out, zoomed in or dim.
Fast (ORB) is lighter on the processor but loses the map more easily.
settings.detectScaleTip: The frame is shrunk to this before it is analysed. Smaller is faster, but a map that is small on screen may no longer be found.
settings.minInliersTip: How many points have to match between the frame and the map before a position is trusted. More turns away false matches but can lose the map on a dim or busy screen.
